title: Rust: Mutex and Shared State
description: Use Mutex and Arc for thread-safe shared state in Rust.

steps.title: Basic Mutex
steps.description: Create a `Mutex<i32>` with value 0. Lock it, increment to 42, and print the value.

verification.failureMessage: Lock Mutex, set to 42, and print.

steps.title: Shared Counter with Arc
steps.description: Create an `Arc<Mutex<i32>>` and share it across 10 threads. Each thread increments the counter 100 times. Print the final value (should be 1000).
hints: Clone Arc before each thread: `let c = Arc::clone(&counter);`.

verification.failureMessage: 10 threads each increment 100 times, final value 1000.

steps.title: Mutex with Complex Data
steps.description: Share a `Vec<i32>` protected by a Mutex across 5 threads. Each thread pushes its ID to the Vec. After joining, print the Vec.
hints: Each thread locks, pushes, and drops.
Threads may interleave, so order varies.

verification.failureMessage: 5 threads each push their ID, print the Vec.

steps.title: Poisoned Mutex
steps.description: Demonstrate a poisoned mutex: spawn a thread that locks a Mutex and panics. In main, try to lock the Mutex and handle `PoisonError`.
hints: When a thread panics while holding a Mutex, it becomes poisoned.
You can recover the value from the poison error.

steps.title: RwLock (Read-Write Lock)
steps.description: Use `RwLock` instead of Mutex. Spawn 3 reader threads and 1 writer thread. Readers call `.read()`, writer calls `.write()`. Print read values.
hints: RwLock is more efficient than Mutex for read-heavy workloads.

verification.failureMessage: Demonstrate RwLock with readers and writer.
